title: "Projr remote compatibility inventory"

Source audit, 23 October 2026. Pinned R source:
[SATVILab/projr 90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397][r-root].
Rust audit baseline: [41cd7b2f][rust-root]; current delivery is listed below,
including the separate [CSV slice PR175][csv-pr].
This inventory was checked against dispatch, config parsing/defaults, store/restore
code, shipped template, documentation and test sources. R tests and live provider
operations were not executed for this audit. A test file is evidence of coverage
intent, not proof of a passing integration run.

**Current source:** explicit local latest/archive listing and staged download,
file-inspected store strategies, native GitHub Release asset/ZIP transfer and
explicit replacement, and configured single-label local/GitHub restore are
implemented. Automatic ordinary publication, metadata-history/cue integration,
default multi-label restore and complete credential-helper parity remain gaps.
The current source features are newer than installed preview.2. CSV capture
does not complete remote parity or M2. CAS is an additional third structure,
not the replacement manifest format or the only archive layout.

Verified delivery: [PR179](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/179),
[PR180](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/180),

passed all12checks and the [pinned gate](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/actions/runs/39944545740):

## Configuration, defaults, aliases and precedence

R destinations are nested at build.local.&lt;title&gt; or build.github.&lt;title&gt;.
Directory sources live at directories.&lt;label&gt;.source, keyed by provider/title,
with string title references or inline mappings understood by restore helpers.
The source-selection helpers contain defects noted below; not every accepted
shape has demonstrated end-to-end behaviour. [Destination storage][dest],
[source getters][source], [restore selection][restore-select].

| Key or entrypoint | Parsed/defaulted/consumed behaviour | Rust status |
|---|---|---|
| Title | Named mapping key. Local helper describes title as descriptive; GitHub title becomes release tag. Internal title helper can derive it from content; public wrappers require the title argument. GitHub wrapper replaces spaces with hyphens. | Configured restore uses named references/inline definitions and GitHub tag space/@version normalization; local title remains descriptive. |
| content | Validates allowed labels; send helper treats null/false as none, true as automatic output/raw/docs, vector as selected labels. Boolean helper support and strict validation are not fully consistent. Cache is not in automatic selection. | Restore accepts false/null, true for declared non-cache roles, or explicit label lists. Build publication remains restricted; no implicit undeclared roles are added. |
| Special content | R option lists also mention docs/data/code/package; wrappers differ in their allowed sets, and code has special ZIP branches. This is not proof each implicit role works through all send paths. | Preserve approved output-r-data and explicit paths. Do not add implicit code/package/language roles merely from enum text; verify actual packaging route separately. |
| structure | archive by default; only archive/latest accepted. The wrapper prose saying version is not a supported alias. | Explicit local/GitHub operations and restore support latest/archive. Configured local latest publication executes; ordinary local archive publication now executes; configured GitHub archive/none/upload-all is a candidate; other combinations remain pending. |
| path | Required for local, anchored at project root when relative. Optional prefix for flat GitHub names. | Local source paths are explicit/root-anchored; compatible GitHub flat-name prefixes exist. |
| path-append-label | Hyphenated YAML key; defaults true. Snake-case path_append_label is an R argument, not evidence of a YAML alias. | Supported by explicit naming/download and configured restore; default true. |
| id | Validator accepts it; completion overwrites local id with path and GitHub id with title. Do not mistake it for a freely configurable independent backend id. | Restore accepts a string id but uses local path/GitHub title, matching completion semantics; it is not an independent routing override. |
| description/id_parent/role | Internal add/check arguments include these legacy fields. Extra-options helper now discards OSF-related extras. No current standalone OSF behaviour follows. | No port required for dead fields without a working source route. |
| send.cue | if-change by default; enum only if-change/always. never occurs in stale wrapper docs but is rejected by current enum. Title-level cue lookup/setter and nested send.cue differ; see defects. | Both nested cues execute in configured local latest with all strategies and inspection modes; archive/GitHub combinations remain pending. |
| send.inspect | manifest by default; file/manifest/none accepted. | Configured local latest supports ordinary MD5 file, default manifest-history comparison/fallback, and none planning. CAS JSON/BLAKE3 checks remain distinct. Ordinary local archive comparison is implemented; configured GitHub publication pending. |
| send.strategy | sync-diff default, except inspect:none defaults upload-all. Explicit upload-missing/upload-all/sync-purge/sync-diff preserved. | Configured local latest supports all four strategies and both cues with CSV/VERSION/changelog updates; actual build/store/restore fixtures cover file, none and trusted manifest actions. Other provider/layout combinations pending. |
| send.conflict | Validator accepts overwrite/skip/error, but no store consumer was found. | Accepted-only R surface, not a functioning conflict-policy requirement. Rust must not silently accept an ineffective control. |
| get.strategy/get.conflict | Accepted/checked; public destination wrappers comment out get arguments. Restore does not consume these policy fields. | Restore rejects nonempty get mappings explicitly instead of pretending the ineffective controls execute. Explicit --clear selects replacement versus merge. |
| source on destination | Restore permits true (preferred), false (exclude), or label vector (preferred for those labels); content must include the label. If absent, first eligible destination is fallback. | Configured restore implements preferences/exclusion/content eligibility with regression fixtures. |
| Per-directory source | Source lookup precedes destination lookup by default; pos can restrict source/dest, type and .title restrict selection. Inline/reference default paths are not uniformly reliable. | Existing source-first references and named inline mappings implemented; indexing/inline source bugs are corrected with fixtures. |
| Settings granularity | Transfer settings are shared per destination title; content labels inherit them. Per-label source mappings choose their own source entries. | Restore resolves per-label sources and shared destination definitions. Complete configured store plans remain missing. |
| YAML layers | Local overrides active profiles overrides base; earlier listed profiles win; merge recurses, null inherits. R uses _projr base/profile/local names. [Merge][merge]. | Core merge precedence exists. Deliberate primary _proj.yml plus legacy _projr.yml conflict error retained. |
| Archive function arguments | archive_local/archive_github accept false/null, true or selected labels; create implicit archive destination only when YAML has no archive title. Existing archive title wins; always_archive controls generated cue. [Send dispatch][send]. | Missing compatibility entrypoints. Do not override explicit YAML silently. |

## Store, inspection and metadata

Production/output builds only enter send; previews skip it. GitHub releases can
be prepared/created before analysis when configured. Destination parameters and
YAML are resolved per title, then labels are processed in content order. Source
files for a send come from the project's current-version manifest, not an
unqualified directory listing. The last label also triggers changelog writing.
[Preparation][prepare], [send][send], [planner][store].

| Policy | Implemented operation | Required Rust fixture |
|---|---|---|
| upload-all | Add every current source-manifest file; no removal of destination-only names. Existing destinations can be marked untrusted. | Existing extra file retained; source overwrite and empty-label cases. |
| upload-missing | Add names absent remotely; retain existing remote bytes, including changed same-name content. | Same-name different bytes retained; missing names added. |
| sync-diff | Add missing/changed files, remove remote-only files; compare via chosen inspection. | Add/change/delete transitions and no-change cue. |
| sync-purge | Clear/recreate destination content then upload full selected set when plan says needed. | Disposable fixture only; never user dataset destructive tests. |
| inspect:file | Enumerate/hash remote bytes with legacy MD5, compare to project evidence. | Detect actual byte corruption and ignore mtime/size equivalence. |
| inspect:manifest | Compare recorded rows/version trust. If unavailable/untrusted, planner may fall back to file hashes. | Matching/missing/stale/corrupt metadata and trust markers. |
| inspect:none | No comparison evidence; default upload-all and untrusted existing-state handling. | Never label unchecked remote bytes verified. |
| cue | always or change-driven materialisation/version updates; no trust or no prior destination can force creation. | Unchanged inputs under both cues; empty result snapshots. |
| Exclusions | Cache inventory excludes projr subtree. File listing includes dotfiles. ZIP helpers accept directory include/exclude and exact filename exclusions; filter implementations differ (pathspec vs regex). | Hidden files, nested names, exclusions and empty-after-exclusion; no regex/pathspec interchange assumption. |
| Execution | Purge, add, remove, reconcile full/empty, then write manifest, VERSION, and optional changelog. | Failure at each boundary must report partial publication honestly. |

[Plan execution][store-execute], [ZIP helpers][zip], [hashing][hash],
[listing/path filters][path].

Local metadata is ordinary manifest.csv, VERSION and CHANGELOG.md at the remote
pre-root. GitHub uses manifest.zip, VERSION.zip and CHANGELOG.zip containing those
files. VERSION has per-label release entries and optional trailing * indicating
untrusted state. These files are distinct from CAS JSON and the plural Rust
.projr/manifests.csv index. [Metadata][metadata].

There is no all-or-nothing remote transaction: local copying/removal can be
partial, GitHub whole-asset replacement deletes an old asset before uploading,
and metadata is written after content. Metadata-download failures may become
empty/unavailable state; some unzip errors are swallowed. Rust should retain
its approved safety boundaries, surface errors and never claim rollback of
remote side effects. [HTTP replacement][http-upload], [GitHub transfer][github].

## Versions, listing, downloads and restore

| Operation | Source behaviour | Rust comparison |
|---|---|---|
| List final remotes | Local immediate child directories; GitHub assets within one configured release. | Explicit local version inspection and GitHub asset listing exist. No cross-release catalogue is promised. |
| List files | Local recursive listing; GitHub ZIP download/extraction. | Local tree staging and ZIP extraction inspect entries; a separate user-facing recursive list-files command is still absent. |
| Latest version | latest reads label VERSION entry; archive parses local version-directory/GitHub asset names and selects max semantic version, including empty variants. | Explicit local listing and configured local/GitHub restore select numeric newest/exact archives or advertised latest. Metadata is not an integrity guarantee; current CAS accepts caller-supplied versions. |
| Trusted version | Stronger helper checks VERSION/archive agreement and project/remote manifest evidence. Restore bypasses this stronger helper. | Missing; do not describe ordinary restore as cryptographically verified. |
| Download all | Copy directory tree or download named release asset and unzip. | Explicit local/asset/directory downloads and configured single-label restore exist, with staging and exact-byte fixtures. |
| Download one | Local and GitHub helpers flatten requested file to its basename at destination. | Missing; basename collision handling needs safe bounded implementation rather than unsafe silent overwrite. |
| Restore labels | Default declared raw labels; explicit labels supported. Root manifest required; empty/unrecorded labels may be skipped. | Root CSV prerequisite and explicit single-label restore exist. Default multi-label raw restore remains missing. |
| Restore source | Source before destination; filter provider/title/content/source eligibility. First suitable selection, not retry across every provider after failure. Legacy fallback GitHub archive then local _archive exists. | Implemented for explicit single-label restore. Source failures do not silently switch providers. Undeclared archive fallbacks are deliberately excluded by the explicit-mapping contract. |
| Restore target | Final declared path, safe=false; optional clear removes current contents before lookup/download. | Declared final target and merge/clear are implemented; stage/validate before installation rather than importing clear-before-lookup data loss. |
| Restore result | Per-label errors can yield partial false; clone wrapper can ignore that false and return true. | Single-label machine results distinguish restored/skipped/failure; stderr retains installation/rollback diagnostics. No multi-label aggregate guarantee is claimed. |
| Clone wrapper | Clone repo, select/change working directory, invoke content update. | Existing Git-backed init is not a restore clone wrapper. |
| Most recently modified | Explicit unimplemented helpers; OSF variants explicitly unsupported. | Do not advertise working modification-time source selection. |

[Version logic][versions], [restore][restore], [clone wrappers][clone].

## Credentials and dependencies

GitHub lower helpers accept explicit token/api_url. Otherwise token lookup is
GITHUB_PAT, optional R gh::gh_token, optional gitcreds, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN.
API base is explicit override, GITHUB_API_URL, public API. Enterprise gitcreds
lookup strips /api/v3; public lookup uses https://github.com. Requests carry an
Authorization header and may be unauthenticated without a token. Repository
inference prefers origin then first Git remote, using available gh R helpers or
system Git/gert. Explicit Enterprise overrides are not forwarded by every wrapper.
[Authentication][auth], [repo inference][repo], [HTTP][http].

These are source mechanisms, not authorisation to obtain new credentials, change
permissions or install dependencies. Rust should use supported existing access,
mock HTTP for fixtures, redact secrets and never store tokens in CSV/URLs.
Current Rust transport accepts explicit API/token inputs; configured restore uses
GITHUB_API_URL and existing GITHUB_PAT/GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN values. Explicit
repository selection avoids Git; inference currently uses origin only and checks
its host against the API. R gh/gitcreds fallback and first-other-remote inference
remain missing. R helper auto-install behaviour is not adopted. Real Git remains an optional
installed dependency; GitHub CLI is separate and need not be mandatory for an
API implementation. Optional managed Git is not planned by default.

## Source defects and documentation-only surfaces

These are source-review findings, not executed reproductions or requirements to
copy bugs. Keep claims bounded until fixture evidence exists.

- Default source selection passes an inner mapping where the next helper expects
  the provider mapping; explicit provider selection can call a title-specific
  helper with a null title. [Selection][restore-select].
- GitHub existence checks hard-code label/version names, ignoring some custom
  path/append-label settings; local archive discovery assumes a label directory.
  [GitHub existence][github-exists], [version paths][versions].
- Title send-check reads top-level cue while defaults populate send.cue; the cue
  setter also writes a different level. [Send][send], [defaults][dest-default].
- get/conflict fields are validated but no effective execution consumer was
  found. wrapper docs mention never/version and OSF, outside actual enums.
- GitHub unzip failures can be swallowed, clone restore ignores partial failure,
  and low-level asset deletion can infer the current repo despite a repo argument.
  [GitHub][github], [HTTP][http], [clone][clone].
- Content option sets, wrapper checks and boolean auto-content helpers differ;
  special code/package labels alone do not prove working end-to-end export.


## Critical configuration assessment, separate from compatibility

This assessment excludes the agreed temporary CSV choice. Examples use the
existing R inline build configuration, not a newly approved Rust schema.
Findings are source-backed; unless stated otherwise they are not executed
reproductions. Proposed fixes are review candidates, not silent semantic changes.

| Rank/type | Example and user impact | Smallest proposed fix |
|---|---|---|
| High: ineffective accepted setting | A destination with send: {conflict: skip} passes allowed-value checks, but store execution never reads conflict. get: {strategy: upload-missing, conflict: error} similarly has no restore consumer. Users can believe a non-overwrite policy is enforced. [Checks][remote-check], [execution][store-execute]. | Reject ineffective combinations until implemented, or implement and test them explicitly. Do not silently ignore a safety control. |
| High: colliding-target combination | build.local.shared with content: [raw-a, raw-b], structure: latest, path-append-label: false, send: {inspect: file, strategy: sync-diff} gives both labels one physical directory. File inspection can classify the other label's files as extras. Custom archive/pre-root paths also assume layouts not uniformly supported. [Layout][layout], [planner][store], [versions][versions]. | Resolve all target identities before mutation and reject collisions; verify supported custom-prefix/append combinations rather than accepting untested layouts. |
| High: destructive restore ordering | A normal configured restore source plus projr_content_update(clear=TRUE) clears the destination before source resolution/download. A missing release or failed network call can leave data gone. clear defaults FALSE; this is an unsafe opt-in ordering, not an unsafe default. [Restore][restore]. | Download into private staging, validate, then apply guarded promotion. Preserve current data on lookup/download failure. |
| Medium: surprising default synchronisation | build.local.shared: {path: backup, structure: latest, content: [output]} defaults to sync-diff, so remote-only files can be removed. A user expecting an additive backup may be surprised. Default archive keeps prior version directories, which narrows the risk. [Defaults][dest-default], [planner][store]. | Clearly expose adds/removes and the resolved strategy before applying; require deliberate review before changing defaults. This is a usability/policy concern, not evidence that sync-diff itself is defective. |
| Medium: profile cannot disable with null | Base build.github.archive selects output; a local/profile build.github.archive: null inherits the base mapping. Removing one active-profile destination also does not remove its base definition. [Merge][merge]. | Explain merged effective destinations and provide a deliberately designed disabling/empty-selection mechanism. Do not reinterpret null without an approved compatibility change. |
| Medium: argument precedence surprise | YAML build.local.archive: {content: [raw-a], path: backup} means archive_local=c('raw-b') does not replace that archive definition. always_archive also defers to explicit archive YAML. [Dispatch][send]. | Document this as YAML authority and display the resolved content; avoid presenting these arguments as ordinary overrides. Whether arguments should override is a design choice. |
| Medium: two cue locations | send: {cue: always} is completed and used per label, while title-level send checking and the setter reference top-level cue. This invites inconsistent getter/setter behaviour; nested cue is not simply unused. [Send][send], [defaults][dest-default]. | Use one canonical nested location and test the public setter through an actual store plan; treat an alias only through explicit conflict rules. |
| Medium: provider-dependent identity | build.github.nightly: {id: another-tag, content: [output]} validates an id, but completion resets it to nightly. Local id instead becomes path. Title is cosmetic locally and functional on GitHub. [Completion][dest-default]. | Reject or clearly deprecate ignored id values; document title/tag/path meanings. A larger unified identity design is separate. |
| Medium: source-selection defects | directories.raw-data.source: {github: archive}, as shipped in the template, meets default helper paths that pass the wrong mapping level or an absent title into a title-specific branch. [Template][template], [selection][restore-select]. | Fix source selection with explicit/default provider/title fixtures; do not require users to discover accidental nesting workarounds. |
| Medium: unsupported documentation | send.cue: never and structure: version are mentioned in wrappers but excluded by current enums; old OSF prose outlives implementation. [Wrappers][wrappers], [enums][options]. | Correct docs and errors. Implement new values only if separately requested, not to make stale prose true. |
| Already recorded design | Removing a build destination can remove a historical restore source because definitions and upload selection share the same location. | The user-requested registry proposal is already [issue706][registry], design-only. It is not a new discovery here and is not implemented by this audit. |
| Low: naming preference | dest versus destinations changes readability, not provider or safety behaviour. | Choose during the existing registry discussion; no new alias or migration silently introduced. |

Credential lookup also deserves explicit presentation: ambient R gh/gitcreds
resolution precedes GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN, and repository inference may choose
origin or the first remote. A supplied environment token or repository can
therefore differ from a user's expectation. The smallest safe improvement is
clear resolved host/repository diagnostics without secrets, plus tests for
explicit overrides; no new credential permissions are implied.

## Test evidence and bounded implementation sequence

[Test sources](https://github.com/SATVILab/projr/tree/90be50132d16aee33e39c0f7f35ef906c35f5397/tests/testthat)
were inspected without running R. Fixtures must establish behaviour before fixes
are claimed; a source test title alone is not an acceptance result.

| Source coverage | What it establishes here |
|---|---|
| test-yml-dest, test-yml-dest-wrapper, test-yml-remote-check | Parser/default/helper assertions exist, including accepted values. Not run in this audit. |
| test-dest-send, test-dest-send-label, test-dest-send-prepare | Dispatch/planner/version/empty helper coverage exists. Not whole-provider publication evidence. |
| test-remote-dispatcher, test-remote-local, test-remote-versions-local | Local dispatcher/layout/transfer/version fixtures exist. Reproduce equivalent Rust fixtures remotely. |
| test-remote-github | Tests require mutable credentials and explicitly skip GitHub Actions. Presence is not CI coverage. Prefer safe mocked REST/ZIP fixtures for Rust. |
| test-restore, test-restore-coverage, test-restore-repo | Restore selection/validation/clone test intent; source defects above still require targeted witnesses. |
| Existing Rust CAS tests | Prove bounded BLAKE3 object/JSON/index behaviour, not ordinary latest/archive parity. |
| PR175 CSV tests | Production pre/post MD5/history, strict encoding, exclusions and recovery; separate exact-head CI/review evidence on that PR. |

Remaining slices should stay independently testable:

1. Configured ordinary publication: cue/inspection policies, shared metadata
   history updates, empty-variant reconciliation and all-destination namespace
   preflight before mutation. Existing explicit transfer commands are foundations,
   not evidence that this combined lifecycle already runs.
2. Remaining restore conveniences and compatibility: default multi-label raw
   restore, individual-file extraction, credential-helper fallback and repository
   inference beyond origin. Retain source-first selection and guarded installation.
3. CAS-specific archive integration where the existing structures do not decide
   snapshot discovery/retention. Isolate those decisions from ordinary parity;
   issue706's future registry remains design-only.

The full inventory stays open until implemented and independently reviewed
evidence maps every supported row. CSV completion alone closes none of the
broader provenance/remote milestones. The future registry proposal is separate
planned work; do not silently implement it while porting old inline definitions.

## Current command reference

See the [remote command reference](cli/remote.qmd) for the delivered local
inspection/download/store, GitHub asset/ZIP/replacement and configured restore
commands, limits and failure boundaries. The [compatibility log](compatibility.qmd)
retains per-slice source comparisons, review findings and verification evidence.

Machine restore stdout has a static structured failure. Stderr carries the
operational diagnostic chain, including paths and parser details; it is not a
general configuration-redaction boundary. HTTP errors omit credentials and
response bodies. Empty/unrecorded labels skip without clearing, and successful
CSV/version selection is not a byte-integrity guarantee.



## Configured local publication candidate

The next bounded slice integrates build.local latest/file with the build's
existing release boundary: current CSV-selected staging, all four file strategies,
both cues, namespace preflight and shared CSV/VERSION/changelog updates.
See the [control matrix](cli/remote.qmd#configured-local-publication-candidate).
[PR185](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/pull/185) records exact-head
independent review and remote verification. File and none inspection are delivered in PR185/188; the current manifest slice
adds the existing default comparison and fallback. Archive comparison selection
and configured GitHub publication remain pending.

Pinned R comparison: dest-send-label.R355,854-1560,1587-1788 and manifest.R67-75,192-225
in the source revision linked above. New empty labels and file-equal missing/starred
metadata receive explicit discoverability corrections; these are documented
differences rather than claims that the pinned R no-change path already repairs
them. No registry or unresolved retention/default policy is adopted.


Local archive publication is the current incremental slice: complete versioned
snapshots, historical reuse eligibility and actual build/store/restore matrix.
Its PR records exact-head review/CI evidence. Configured GitHub publication and
configured append-label:false remain pending; no full remote-completion claim.


Configured GitHub latest/archive publication supports file/manifest/none inspection and all four strategies,
including missing Release creation, CSV data ZIPs and shared metadata history.
Canonical current-data replacement merges selected files while preserving remote
extras. Empty sources preserve existing targets; validated empty-to-full transitions
remove the obsolete sentinel asset after upload. Its PR records mocked REST CLI
round-trip evidence. File/manifest and historical comparison use the same staged
ordinary planner as local remotes; the command reference records the full control
matrix and source-backed blind missing/diff and bounded purge interactions.
No live GitHub Release round-trip has been performed.


The comparison candidate preserves the existing archive/manifest/sync-diff/
if-change defaults. Reuse requires newest catalog/VERSION/matching CSV agreement
and continuous unchanged history. Physical file fallback, trusted partial manifest
semantics, complete new snapshots and corrupt-empty rejection have actual CLI
mock REST regression fixtures. Exact-head remote CI and independent review remain
required; this does not complete all provider options or live GitHub validation.
